summary: What survives checking: (1) Taipei data show motorcycle riders get the highest commuter PM2.5 (MOENV 2017: 32.1 vs 7.6 ug/m3 in cars) and that walking or riding PM2.5 in Taipei is associated with small short-term blood-pressure and heart-rate rises in healthy adults (Chuang 2020, association only). (2) International studies, all UK, Hong Kong or Shanghai and mostly car or diesel based, agree that junction particle peaks occur as vehicles decelerate and pull away from stops, with ultrafine number peaks up to 29x free-flow in a diesel test car (Goel & Kumar 2015) but PM2.5 mass only about 16% higher (Kumar & Goel 2016). (3) The lowest air is the worst: fine particles up to 44% higher at pram height (Sharma & Kumar 2020), ~40% lower at 4.7 m than at street level at one junction. (4) Marking rules allow a turn box edge 50 cm from the crosswalk. Not established: any Taiwanese red-versus-green or kerb-versus-mid-block measurement for scooters; the IOT intersection report could not be opened by this checker, so its figures, including 94%, are unverified. The peak is at pull-away, so the idle-at-red framing must be hedged.

findings.claim: 120 healthy Taipei adults: PM2.5 highest in scooter mode (53.6 +/- 26.1 ug/m3, subway 21.7 +/- 5.8); PM2.5 associated with higher SBP, HR and urinary 8-OHdG in walking and scooter modes; no significant PM2.5-BP-HR association when walking with a facemask.
findings.setting: Taipei, 120 healthy adults, six modes, 09:00-10:00
findings.citation: Chuang K-J, Lin L-Y, Ho K-F, Su C-T, 2020. Traffic-related PM2.5 exposure and its cardiovascular effects among healthy commuters in Taipei, Taiwan. Atmospheric Environment: X 7:100084.
findings.quote: personal exposure to PM2.5 was associated with increased SBP (W: 6.5%; Sc: 7.9%), HR (W: 3.4%; Sc: 6.4%) and urinary 8-OHdG (W: 8.1%; Sc: 8.9%) in the walking (W) mode and scooter (Sc) mode
findings.caveats: Association, not proof of causation. The abstract does not state the exposure increment the percentages refer to. 'Scooter mode' means riding a scooter, not standing near one. Walking mode is general street walking, not waiting at a red light. Short-term biomarkers in healthy adults, not disease. The facemask finding in the abstract concerns BP and HR only.
findings.useOnSite: Say 'in 120 healthy Taipei commuters, higher personal PM2.5 while walking or riding a scooter was associated with small short-term rises in blood pressure, heart rate and a DNA-damage marker'.
findings.verifierNote: Paper, authors, numbers confirmed via Crossref and OpenAlex abstract. Corrected: the facemask result covers BP and HR only (not 8-OHdG), and the percentage increments have no stated unit in the abstract.
findings.design: See original researcher note; abstract or full text re-checked by verifier where verdict is not UNREACHABLE.

findings.claim: Taipei volunteers with a portable PM2.5 detector: median 40 (10-275) walking along streets; bus 35; car 15; motorcycle 75 (60-105) ug/m3.
findings.setting: Taipei metropolitan area
findings.citation: Wang C-Y, Lim B-S, Wang Y-H, Huang Y-C T, 2021. Identification of High Personal PM2.5 Exposure during Real Time Commuting in the Taipei Metropolitan Area. Atmosphere 12(3):396.
findings.quote: Exposure to PM2.5 (median (range)) was higher when walking along the streets (40 (10–275) µg/m3) compared to riding the buses (35 (13–65) µg/m3) and the cars (15 (8–80) µg/m3)
findings.caveats: No sample size or signal-phase data in the abstract. Underground MRT (80) was as high as or higher than street walking, and temples (588 +/- 271) and a night-market food court (405 +/- 238) were much higher, from cooking and incense, not traffic. The abstract does NOT say where the 275 walking maximum came from; the first researcher's suggestion that it reflects temples is speculation. Motorcycle was compared against walking (p<0.0001).
findings.useOnSite: Say 'volunteers measuring PM2.5 on Taipei streets found a wide range (median 40, up to 275 ug/m3), higher than inside cars (15)'. Do not attribute the high values to traffic or to temples.
findings.verifierNote: Numbers confirmed from the abstract. Corrected: removed the unsupported claim that the 275 maximum may come from temples (temples were a separate, higher category); added that underground MRT readings were also high.
findings.design: See original researcher note; abstract or full text re-checked by verifier where verdict is not UNREACHABLE.

findings.claim: Roadside PNSD and VOC measurements near a traffic nexus in a subtropical urban area, spring-summer 2021: traffic fell 20-27% while early-morning motorcycle activity surged.
findings.value: traffic -20% to -27%
findings.setting: Subtropical urban area; city not named in abstract; 2021
findings.citation: Chen T-L, Hsiao T-C, Chen A-Y, Chang K-E, Lin T-C, Griffith S M, Chou C C-K, 2024. A traffic-induced shift of ultrafine particle sources under COVID-19 soft lockdown in a subtropical urban area. Environment International 187:108658.
findings.quote: a 20-27% dip in overall traffic yet a surprising surge in early morning motorcycle activity
findings.caveats: The abstract says lower primary traffic emissions amplified the role of aged particles and secondary aerosols, and that stagnant conditions with reduced dilution exacerbated the influence of alternative sources, 'notably solvent evaporation', not traffic. It does not show that weak dilution raised traffic UFP at the roadside, has no red/green analysis and no pedestrian exposure.
findings.useOnSite: Do not use for red-light or pedestrian claims. At most: Taiwanese roadside work finds that when dilution is weak, local non-exhaust sources such as solvents matter more.
findings.verifierNote: Paper and authors confirmed (Crossref, Europe PMC). Corrected the first researcher's paraphrase: stagnation amplified solvent-evaporation sources, not traffic exhaust.
findings.design: See original researcher note; abstract or full text re-checked by verifier where verdict is not UNREACHABLE.

findings.claim: Car-based mobile measurements at 10 Guildford signalised intersections: peak particle number during red-light delay up to 29x the free-flow average; ~2% of commuting time at intersections gave ~25% of respiratory dose.
findings.value: peak PNC up to 29x free-flow average; 2% of time ~25% of RDD (a single run: 27 s of delay = 2% of that run, 25% of its RDD); average RDD rate during delay up to 7x the rest of the run
findings.setting: Guildford, UK (non-Taiwanese); test car was a 2002 diesel Ford Fiesta; DMS50 at 10 Hz, 5-560 nm; 6 km route
findings.citation: Goel A, Kumar P, 2015. Characterisation of nanoparticle emissions and exposure at traffic intersections through fast-response mobile and sequential measurements. Atmospheric Environment 107:374-390.
findings.quote: Short-term exposure for ~2% of total commuting time in car corresponded to ~25% of total respiratory doses. (full text: peak PNCs at TIs during delay events were up to 29-times higher than average PNCs under free-flow conditions)
findings.caveats: Car occupant, not pedestrian; UK petrol and diesel traffic, not scooters. The 29x compares PEAK delay values with the free-flow AVERAGE (the paper's conclusion loosely says 'average PNCs ... up to 29-times'; its results text says peak). The largest values arose when the test car accelerated close to the tailpipe of a preceding vehicle, including old diesel cars. The 2%/25% worked example comes from run 19. Particle number, not mass. Highest particle counts occurred when vehicles accelerated from idle, not during idling.
findings.useOnSite: Say 'in a UK study of a car driving through 10 junctions, brief peaks of ultrafine particle number during stop-and-go delay reached up to 29 times the free-flow average; pedestrians and scooters were not measured'.
findings.verifierNote: Read the Surrey repository full text. 2%/25% and 29x are present, but 29x is a peak-over-average ratio, 2%/25% is a single-run example generalised in the abstract, and the vehicle was diesel. Wording tightened.
findings.design: See original researcher note; abstract or full text re-checked by verifier where verdict is not UNREACHABLE.

findings.claim: UK mobile and fixed-site study: on-road median PM10, PM2.5, PM1 during intersection delays ~40%, 16%, 17% higher than free-flow; ~7% of commuting time in delay = 10, 7, 8% of RDD; in-car PM10 RDD with windows open up to ~7x pedestrian RDD.
findings.value: PM10 +40%, PM2.5 +16%, PM1 +17%; in-car PM10 RDD up to ~7x pedestrians
findings.setting: Guildford, UK (non-Taiwanese); 10 intersections, plus fixed sites at a 3-way and a 4-way
findings.citation: Kumar P, Goel A, 2016. Concentration dynamics of coarse and fine particulate matter at and around signalised traffic intersections. Environmental Science: Processes & Impacts 18:1220-1235.
findings.quote: On-road median PM10, PM2.5 and PM1 during delays at the TIs were ∼40%, 16% and 17% higher, respectively, compared with free-flow conditions on the rest of the route.
findings.caveats: The '7 times' applies to PM10 RDD and compares in-car (windows open) with pedestrians; it means pedestrians had LOWER dose than the in-car sampler, so it must not be used to inflate pedestrian risk. Mass shows far smaller excess than particle number. A paper citing this work (He & Gao 2021) reports pedestrian-at-4-way congested-vs-free-flow RDD 7.3x for PM10 and 1.2x for PM2.5, seen only second-hand.
findings.useOnSite: Say 'in this UK study the PM2.5 excess at junction delays was a modest 16%; the larger excess was in ultrafine number'.
findings.verifierNote: Abstract in Europe PMC matches all numbers. Corrected: the ~7x figure is PM10-specific and shows in-car dose exceeding pedestrian dose.
findings.design: See original researcher note; abstract or full text re-checked by verifier where verdict is not UNREACHABLE.

findings.claim: At two Guildford intersections particle number fell exponentially with height (1-4.7 m): ~40% less at 4.7 m than ground at the 4-way site; vertical decay ~132x sharper than along-road; emission factors >10x higher in congestion; 4-way average PNC ~2x the 3-way.
findings.value: ~40% lower at 4.7 m; ~132x; PNEF >10x; RDD up to 14x higher at 4-way congested vs 3-way
findings.setting: Guildford, UK (non-Taiwanese); fixed ~1.5 m, vertical 1-4.7 m, along-road 10-60 m
findings.citation: Goel A, Kumar P, 2016. Vertical and horizontal variability in airborne nanoparticles and their exposure around signalised traffic intersections. Environmental Pollution 214:54-69.
findings.quote: Vertical PNC profiles followed an exponential decay, which was much sharper at 4-way TI than at 3-way TI, suggesting ∼40% less exposure for people at first floor (4.7 m) to those at ground floor around 4-way TI.
findings.caveats: Heights start at 1 m, so it is not a child-vs-adult comparison. Sequential, not simultaneous, sampling. Along-road samples were taken close to moving vehicles, which explains the weak horizontal decay.
findings.useOnSite: Say 'near a UK intersection, ultrafine particle numbers fell with height, about 40% lower at first-floor height than at street level at one site'.
findings.verifierNote: Abstract confirmed in Europe PMC.
findings.design: See original researcher note; abstract or full text re-checked by verifier where verdict is not UNREACHABLE.

findings.caveats: Along-road extent, not distance from the kerb. Deceleration contributed most to PNC at all but one intersection type. Car-based mobile data.

findings.claim: Review: peak particle number at signalised intersections 0.7-5.4 x 10^5 cm-3 vs ~0.3 x 10^5 at typical roadsides; peak RDD at intersections up to 12x roadside.
findings.setting: Review of a few field studies (non-Taiwanese, non-scooter)
findings.citation: Goel A, Kumar P, 2014. A review of fundamental drivers governing the emissions, dispersion and exposure to vehicle-emitted nanoparticles at signalised traffic intersections. Atmospheric Environment 97:316-331.
findings.quote: reporting over an order of magnitude larger peak PNCs (0.7–5.4 ×105 cm–3) compared with average PNCs at typical roadsides (~0.3×105 cm–3)
findings.caveats: The 5.4 x 10^5 top of the range is the Hong Kong heavy-duty diesel bus peak from Tsang et al. 2008, cited in the review's text. Peak-versus-average, 'only a few field studies'. The 12x RDD is based on peak PNC.
findings.useOnSite: Say 'a review found short-lived particle-number peaks at junctions over ten times typical roadside averages, mostly from studies of diesel-influenced traffic'.
findings.verifierNote: Read the Surrey full text; numbers match. Added the caveat that the upper bound is the diesel-bus peak.

findings.claim: Instruments in a pram on a 2.7 km Guildford route with 4 intersections: at intersections PNC 62-68% higher, PM2.5 7-10% higher, PM2.5-10 10-19% higher than the rest of the route.
findings.setting: Guildford, UK (non-Taiwanese); 64 trips, ~87 km, school drop-off and pick-up hours
findings.citation: Kumar P, Rivas I, Sachdeva L, 2017. Exposure of in-pram babies to airborne particles during morning drop-in and afternoon pick-up of school children. Environmental Pollution 224:407-420.
findings.quote: PM2.5, PM2.5-10 and PNCs during the morning (afternoon) at TIs were 7 (10)%, 19 (10)% and 68 (62)% higher, respectively, compared with the rest of the route.
findings.caveats: PNC in this study is particle number in the 0.2-1 um range, i.e. not the ultrafine fraction (<0.1 um), although the abstract loosely says 'including ultrafine particles'. Road salt and brake wear were identified; not scooter exhaust. Intersection segments are not split into red and green. Note that the first researcher's 'about 60-70% higher ultrafine particle numbers' is not supported.
findings.useOnSite: Say 'in the UK, instruments carried in a pram recorded about 60-70% higher particle number (0.2-1 um) at junctions than elsewhere on the route'.
findings.verifierNote: Abstract confirmed. Corrected the size class: 0.2-1 um particle number, not ultrafine.
findings.design: See original researcher note; abstract or full text re-checked by verifier where verdict is not UNREACHABLE.

findings.claim: Simultaneous UK measurements: in-pram fine particle concentration up to 44% higher than at adult breathing height; double-pram bottom seat PNC ~72% higher than top; covers cut fine particles up to 39%.
findings.value: up to +44% fine; +72% PNC bottom seat; covers -39% fine, -43% coarse; PNC varied up to 290x within a run
findings.setting: Guildford, UK (non-Taiwanese); 89 runs, 2.1 km, 66 h, 145 km
findings.citation: Sharma A, Kumar P, 2020. Quantification of air pollution exposure to in-pram babies and mitigation strategies. Environment International 139:105671.
findings.quote: The average in-pram concentration of fine particles was always higher by up to 44% compared with adult breathing height during both morning and afternoon runs.
findings.caveats: 'Up to' maximum; a walking route, not an intersection stand; PNC here is <=0.1 um as defined by the authors; brake and tyre wear dominated the coarse fraction at baby height.
findings.useOnSite: Say 'UK measurements found fine particles up to 44% higher at a pram's breathing height than an adult's'.
findings.verifierNote: Abstract confirmed.
findings.design: See original researcher note; abstract or full text re-checked by verifier where verdict is not UNREACHABLE.

findings.quote: The air within the first few meters above the road level is usually most polluted.

findings.claim: Synthesis of 41 roadside studies: most pollutants decay to background by 115-570 m from the road edge; >=50% fall by 150 m for CO and some UFP counts; PM mass shows no trend.
findings.value: 115-570 m (edge normalisation) / 160-570 m (background normalisation)
findings.setting: 41 studies, >700 measurements (mostly US/European roads and highways)
findings.citation: Karner A A, Eisinger D S, Niemeier D A, 2010. Near-roadway air quality: synthesizing the findings from real-world data. Environmental Science & Technology 44(14):5334-5344.
findings.quote: at least a 50% decrease in peak/edge-of-road concentration by 150 m
findings.caveats: Decay over 100s of metres, not the 1-3 m a pedestrian stands from a queue. The abstract does not say 'highways' or 'mostly US/Europe'; that characterisation was not confirmed from the abstract. Silent on scooters.
findings.useOnSite: Say 'roadside studies find many traffic pollutants fall by half within about 150 m of the road'. Do not translate to metres of stop-line distance.
findings.verifierNote: Abstract confirmed. Flagged that the 'mostly highways, US and Europe' description is not in the abstract.

findings.claim: Fixed and mobile measurements at a Shanghai intersection: PM varied periodically with the signal cycle; pedestrian submicron exposure in the crosswalk slightly higher than waiting at the roadside.
findings.value: qualitative
findings.setting: Shanghai, China (non-Taiwanese), beside an elevated road, Oct and Dec 2018 evening peak
findings.citation: He H-D, Gao H O, 2021. Particulate matter exposure at a densely populated urban traffic intersection and crosswalk. Environmental Pollution 268:115931.
findings.quote: At an urban traffic intersection, for example, pedestrians are often at a higher risk of exposure to near-source PM pollution from traffic while waiting on the roadside or while walking in the crosswalk. (abstract)
findings.caveats: The abstract does not contain the 'slightly higher in the crosswalk' result; I did not locate it either, so omit it. From the preprint results text: roadside PM RISES as vehicles start to move on green and then falls during the phases when traffic is stopped. The peak is at pull-away, not during the idle wait. One site, two days, no scooter share given.
findings.useOnSite: Say 'a Shanghai study found roadside particle levels rose and fell with the signal cycle, rising as queued vehicles moved off'. Do not say concentrations are highest while vehicles idle at red.
findings.verifierNote: Read the abstract and the arXiv 2011.09286 full text. Corrected: the signal-cycle pattern shows peaks as traffic starts moving; the crosswalk-vs-roadside claim was not confirmed and is dropped.
findings.design: See original researcher note; abstract or full text re-checked by verifier where verdict is not UNREACHABLE.

findings.claim: Two-week London junction study: extending the signal cycle changed NOx -21% downwind and +23% upwind; pedestrians waiting to cross had a 46% rise in NOx exposure as waiting time rose.
findings.value: +46% NOx exposure with longer waits; -21%/+23% NOx by wind direction; model -23% emissions within 15 m
findings.setting: London, UK (non-Taiwanese), two-week field study
findings.citation: Schroeder A K, Woodward H, Le Cornec C M A, Proust T, et al., 2024. Vehicle emission models alone are not sufficient to understand full impact of change in traffic signal timings. Atmospheric Environment: X 24:100293.
findings.quote: This indicates that meteorology was by far the greatest determinant of roadside concentrations during our two-week study period.
findings.caveats: The 46% is an estimate of pedestrian NOx exposure for waiting pedestrians as waiting times increased, in a model-plus-sensor study. NOx, not scooter PM; not Taiwan.
findings.useOnSite: Say 'wind direction can matter more than signal timing for what a pedestrian breathes; longer waits raised modelled exposure for waiting pedestrians'.
findings.verifierNote: Abstract confirmed via OpenAlex.
findings.design: See original researcher note; abstract or full text re-checked by verifier where verdict is not UNREACHABLE.

findings.claim: Under MOTC marking rules: scooter stop box (機慢車停等區) depth 2.5-6 m; two-stage turn box rear edge >=0.5 m from the crosswalk (adjustable); crosswalk generally 3-5 m from the cross-road edge.
findings.value: stop box 2.5-6 m deep; turn box rear edge >=0.5 m from crosswalk; crosswalk 3-5 m from cross-road edge
findings.setting: Taiwan national rule, Laws and Regulations Database
findings.citation: 交通部, 道路交通標誌標線號誌設置規則, Arts. 174-2, 185, 191.
findings.quote: 待轉區後緣應與行人穿越道線間隔五十公分以上。但不影響行人穿越安全時，得依實際情形酌予調整。
findings.caveats: Minimums and design principles; actual layouts vary. Art. 174-2: the stop box sits behind the stop line (停止線後方) on roads at or below 60 km/h with signals; the stop-line-to-crosswalk gap is not in these articles, so no typical distance from the stop box to pedestrians is established. The turn box is drawn in front of the crosswalk, inside the junction (Art. 191). Art. 185-1 provides diagonal crosswalk markings for pedestrian-exclusive phases. I did not re-check the database's amendment date.
findings.useOnSite: Say 'the national marking rules require the scooter turn box to be at least 50 cm from the crosswalk, adjustable, and set the scooter stop box depth at 2.5-6 m'.
findings.verifierNote: Downloaded the law page and read Arts. 174-2, 185, 191; the quoted text and figures match.
findings.design: See original researcher note; abstract or full text re-checked by verifier where verdict is not UNREACHABLE.

findings.claim: Field measurements in six Taipei street canyons (aspect ratio one): PM2.5 and PM10 sometimes correlated with canyon structure, sometimes dominated by meso-scale processes; CO and O3 inversely correlated.
findings.value: qualitative
findings.setting: Taipei City, six street canyons, hot and cool days
findings.citation: Lin B-S, Chang H-C, Chen C-W, Huang I-H, Pardthaisong L, Hsieh C-I, 2024. Effects of Street Spatial Structure on Micrometeorological Condition and Air Quality: A Case Study of Taipei City. Forests 15(12):2221.
findings.quote: in some cases, concentrations of PM2.5 and PM10 were found to be correlated with local street canopy structure; however, in some cases, the meso-scale process was found to be the dominant factor
findings.caveats: Mainly a thermal comfort and micrometeorology paper. Does not show canyons trap scooter exhaust; no arcades or inversions.
findings.useOnSite: Do not use as evidence canyons trap exhaust.
findings.verifierNote: Abstract confirmed. Corrected the author list (six authors, adding Pardthaisong and Hsieh; first researcher listed four).

findings.claim: Hanoi pilot study: motorcyclists have much higher black carbon exposure than other commuters.
findings.value: BC on motorcycles mean 29.4 ug/m3 vs 10.1 in buses; peak traffic 34.7 vs 12.1; off-peak 27.7 vs 8.4; car cabin 18.1 (windows open) and 11.7 (closed)
findings.setting: Hanoi, Vietnam; microAeth AE51 on motorcycles and in car and bus cabins; pilot study
findings.citation: Quang T N, Hue N T, Dat M V, Tran L K, Phi T, Morawska L, Thai P, 2021. Motorcyclists have much higher exposure to black carbon compared to other commuters in traffic of Hanoi, Vietnam. Atmospheric Environment 245:118029.
findings.quote: The mean BC concentration on motorcycles was 29.4 μg/m3 compared to 10.1 μg/m3 in the buses.
findings.caveats: Pilot study of riders, not pedestrians at intersections. BC levels in Hanoi riders reflect close proximity to the traffic stream. Sample size not read.
findings.useOnSite: Say 'a pilot study in Hanoi found riders breathing about three times the black carbon of bus passengers (29.4 vs 10.1 ug/m3)'. Do not apply to pedestrians.
findings.verifierNote: Upgraded from SECONDARY: abstract retrieved via Semantic Scholar and numbers read. Author spelling per the source is Quang Ngoc Tran.
findings.design: See original researcher note; abstract or full text re-checked by verifier where verdict is not UNREACHABLE.

doNotClaim: Do not say a red-light scooter pack raises pedestrian PM2.5 by 94%, or cite 94% at all until the IOT PDF is opened; per the first researcher it is a best-case modelled reduction from one day at one site.
Do not say Taiwanese measurements show intersection air is X times worse than mid-block or green phase; no such Taiwanese study was found.
Do not use the Goel and Kumar 29x, 2%/25% or 7x figures as pedestrian or scooter numbers: car occupant, UK, diesel test car, peak-over-average, 2%/25% from one run.
Do not present any Hong Kong or review peak (5.4 x 10^5 cm-3) as scooter exhaust; it was a diesel bus.
Do not say concentrations are highest while scooters idle at red: the Shanghai and Hong Kong papers and Goel and Kumar put the peak at acceleration from stops.
Do not call the Kumar 2017 pram particle number 'ultrafine'; it was 0.2-1 um.
Do not present UK pram figures (44%, 72%, 62-68%) as Taiwanese stroller measurements.
Do not say that waiting at a Taiwanese red light causes illness in children or older people; Chuang 2020 is an association in healthy adults with short-term biomarkers.
Do not say the smell proves a harmful dose.
Do not attribute Wang 2021's 275 ug/m3 walking maximum to temples or traffic.
Do not claim Chen 2024 shows weak dilution raised traffic exhaust at roadsides; it points to solvent sources.
Do not claim arcades, street canyons or inversions trap exhaust at pedestrian level in Taiwan; no Taiwanese measurement found.
Do not state a typical stop-box-to-crosswalk distance or pedestrian red time; neither is documented in verified sources.

Metre-scale distance decay for scooter exhaust at a kerb is missing; Karner 2010 covers 100s of metres.
Scooters queued per red light and pedestrian red times for Taipei, New Taipei, Taichung and Kaohsiung are unpublished in what was verified.
Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City and Bangkok intersection or red-light queue studies: none found; the Hanoi BC study is of riders.
Kumar and Goel 2016 pedestrian RDD ratios (7.3x PM10, 1.2x PM2.5 congested vs free-flow at the 4-way) were seen only second-hand via He and Gao and should be checked in the full paper.
